from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Music relies on a steady pulse called the beat.", 
                         "Fractions represent how long each note lasts.", 
                         "A whole note lasts the full beat."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Pulse of Time", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define visual elements
        center_T = Dot(color=WHITE).scale(2)
        label_T = Text("T", color=WHITE, font_size=24).next_to(center_T, UP)
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(center_T, label_T), 'C3')
        
        clock_hand = Line(start=center_T.get_center(), end=center_T.get_center() + UP * 1.5, color=BLUE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(center_T), Write(label_T))
        self.play(Create(clock_hand))
        self.play(Rotate(clock_hand, angle=2*PI, about_point=center_T.get_center(), run_time=3))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        pulse = Circle(radius=0.2, color=WHITE).move_to(center_T.get_center())
        self.play(FadeIn(pulse))
        self.play(pulse.animate.scale(3).set_color("#FFD700"), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        time_text = Text("Time is discrete", color="#00FFFF", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(time_text, 'E3')
        self.play(Write(time_text))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(3)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Notes fill measures like water in a vessel.", "Each note occupies specific rhythmic space.", "They must sum to the measure's total capacity."]

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Dynamic Application: Changing Meters", [
            "Different time signatures change the musical feel.",
            "A 4/4 march feels structured and heavy.",
            "A 3/4 waltz spins in a circle."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        meter_a = VGroup(
            Square(color="#FF69B4", fill_opacity=0.5),
            Text("4/4", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        )
        meter_b = VGroup(
            Circle(color="#7B68EE", fill_opacity=0.5),
            Text("3/4", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.wait(3)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF69B4")
        self.place_at_grid(meter_a, "C2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(meter_a))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#7B68EE")
        self.place_at_grid(meter_b, "C5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(meter_b))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Swap positions
        self.play(
            meter_a.animate.move_to(self.grid["C5"]),
            meter_b.animate.move_to(self.grid["C2"]),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis & Summary", [
            "Beat is the unit of time.",
            "Measure is the container for notes.",
            "Time signature sets the rhythmic rule."
        ])

        # Objects
        beat_circle = Circle(radius=0.5, color=YELLOW)
        beat_label = Text("Beat", font_size=20).next_to(beat_circle, DOWN)
        beat_group = VGroup(beat_circle, beat_label)
        
        measure_box = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=BLUE)
        measure_label = Text("Measure", font_size=20).next_to(measure_box, DOWN)
        measure_group = VGroup(measure_box, measure_label)
        
        rule_text = MathTex(r"4/4", font_size=36, color=GREEN)
        rule_label = Text("Rule", font_size=20).next_to(rule_text, DOWN)
        rule_group = VGroup(rule_text, rule_label)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(beat_group, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(beat_group), wait_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(measure_group, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(measure_group), wait_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(rule_group, "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(rule_group), wait_time=2)
        
        self.play(
            beat_group.animate.shift(LEFT*1),
            measure_group.animate.shift(RIGHT*1),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Rhythm of Mathematics: Understanding Music and Measure Theory
outline.target_audience: High school students interested in music theory and STEM

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Pulse of Time
sections.content: Define 'Beat' as the fundamental unit of time. Introduce the concept of a 'Fraction' as the mathematical basis for musical duration (Whole, Half, Quarter, Eighth notes).
sections.example: A mechanical owl's steady 'tick-tock' representing the constant beat, while its wings represent fractions of that time (1 full wing flap = 1 beat, half-flap = 1/2 beat).

sections.title: Defining the Measure (The Container)
sections.content: Explain that music is organized into 'Measures' (or bars) using Time Signatures. Introduce the Time Signature as a fraction where the numerator is beats per measure and the denominator is the note value that equals one beat.
sections.example: A visual animation of a 'Musical Basket' that can only hold a sum of 4/4 beats. If the basket is full, a wall appears, forcing the next notes into a new basket (measure).

sections.title: Visualizing Measure Theory
sections.content: Apply graphic representations to show how notes fill a measure like water filling a vessel. Use a stacked bar graph to demonstrate that different note lengths must sum up to the total capacity defined by the time signature.
sections.example: An animation of a robot composer placing blocks of different lengths into a slot; the blocks must equal exactly 4 units wide to fit perfectly into the '4/4 measure frame'.

sections.title: Dynamic Application: Changing Meters
sections.content: Briefly demonstrate how changing the time signature changes the 'gravity' or the feeling of the music. Contrast 4/4 (march) with 3/4 (waltz) using geometric shapes.
sections.example: A bouncy character jumping on tiles: in 4/4, they land on tiles 1 and 3 (heavy); in 3/4, they land on a triangle path, creating a circular, spinning rhythm.

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary
sections.content: Review: Beat = Unit, Measure = Container, Time Signature = Rule. Connect musical measures to periodic functions in mathematics.
sections.example: A final visual showing a Sine Wave overlaying a musical staff, where the peaks of the wave align perfectly with the start of every measure.
